Clinical details:
Palpitations. Brother diagnosed with dilated cardiomyopathy aged 41. ?Familial cardiomyopathy.

Technique:
Cardiac MRI at 1.5 T. Cine SSFP imaging in standard long- and short-axis planes, T2-weighted STIR, native T1 and T2 mapping, post-contrast T1 mapping and late gadolinium enhancement imaging following 0.1 mmol/kg gadobutrol.

Findings:
The left ventricle is normal in size and wall thickness with preserved systolic function and no regional wall motion abnormality. LVEDVi 88 ml/m², LVESVi 33 ml/m², LVEF 62%, LV mass index 58 g/m².

The right ventricle is normal in size with preserved systolic function. RVEDVi 92 ml/m², RVESVi 40 ml/m², RVEF 57%.

The atria are not dilated. No significant valvular regurgitation or stenosis.

No pericardial effusion. No significant extracardiac findings.

Tissue characterisation:
Native T1 985 ms (local reference range 950–1050 ms at 1.5 T). T2 48 ms (local reference range 42–52 ms). ECV 26% (normal <30%). No myocardial oedema.

Late gadolinium enhancement:
No late gadolinium enhancement. No intracardiac thrombus.

Conclusion:
Normal cardiac MRI. No evidence of cardiomyopathy.
